prompt: What does PASTA stand for?

choices.text: Policy, Assets, Systems, Threats, Actions
choices.why: Invented.

choices.text: Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Prioritised Attack Surface Threat Assessment
choices.why: Close words, wrong method.

choices.text: Penetration and Security Testing Approach
choices.why: PASTA is not a pentest.

prompt: What makes PASTA risk-centric, in the lesson's terms?

choices.text: It uses a different list of threat categories from STRIDE's six
choices.why: Stage 4 can use STRIDE itself.

choices.text: It gives every threat a numeric score from a fixed formula
choices.why: The book prescribes no single formula; lessons 9 to 11 cover the numbers.

choices.text: It is done by the risk team instead of the developers
choices.why: It needs the builders too.

choices.text: It starts and ends with the business
choices.why: Right: stage 1 objectives, stage 7 impact.

prompt: Which stage of PASTA is the work of lesson 2?

choices.text: Stage 3, decomposition
choices.why: Right: the DFD with trust boundaries.

choices.text: Stage 1, objectives
choices.why: That is the business view.

choices.text: Stage 6, attack modelling
choices.why: That draws paths, lesson 5's trees.

choices.text: Stage 2, technical scope
choices.why: Scope lists components; it does not draw flows.

prompt: T03, T12 and T09 are three lines on the STRIDE list. What does the attacker's view see in them?

choices.text: Three unrelated threats of similar weight
choices.why: Read in sequence, they connect.

choices.text: Duplicates to be merged into one line
choices.why: Each has its own fix; the path is what joins them.

choices.text: One path
choices.why: Right: phishing to every clinical note.

choices.text: A reason to run a pentest first
choices.why: Stage 6 maps defences; it does not attack.

prompt: Match each group of PASTA stages to the point of view it takes.
Put the first three stages of PASTA in order.

choices.text: Nine thousand patients have an account on the portal today
choices.why: True, but not the number tied to bookings and payment.

choices.text: Four clinics
choices.why: That does not price a broken booking flow.

choices.text: About 60% of bookings come through the portal
choices.why: Right, and daniel was the one who knew it.

choices.text: Fourteen threats
choices.why: That is stage 4's count.

prompt: Why does stage 2 write down that the clinics' Wi-Fi is out of scope?

choices.text: So the model is not blamed later for what it never covered
choices.why: Right. Out of scope is a decision, and it is recorded.

choices.text: Because Wi-Fi has no threats
choices.why: It has plenty; bruno handles them separately.

choices.text: Because the LGPD excludes networks inside the clinics from any model
choices.why: The law says nothing about Wi-Fi scope.

choices.text: To make the DFD fit on one page
choices.why: Scope is about responsibility, not layout.

prompt: What does PASTA's stage 3 add beside the DFD?

choices.text: A list of CWE identifiers
choices.why: That is stage 5.

choices.text: The business objectives
choices.why: That is stage 1.

choices.text: A ranked list of risks
choices.why: That is stage 7.

choices.text: Use cases
choices.why: Right: each a path stage 6 will read backwards.

prompt: Under the LGPD, health data is classed as ___ personal data.
What did stage 4 add to the fourteen STRIDE threats at Vereda?

choices.text: Ten new threats from threat intelligence reports
choices.why: It added context, not new threats.

choices.text: Which of them somebody is actively trying
choices.why: Right: T02 and the phishing chain moved up.

choices.text: A CWE for each threat
choices.why: That is stage 5.

choices.text: Nothing, since STRIDE already covers the world outside
choices.why: The drawing cannot know what attackers are doing.

prompt: Match each threat to the weakness stage 5 named for it.
Why are weaknesses named with CWE in stage 5?

choices.text: So model, scanner and pentest findings join on one identifier
choices.why: Right. The join is the point.

choices.text: Because the LGPD requires CWE numbers
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: To score each weakness
choices.why: CWE names; it does not score.

choices.text: Because CVE only covers hardware
choices.why: CVE names known vulnerabilities in software.

prompt: Stage 5 finds no weakness for T08, the SMS text. How is it recorded?

choices.text: As closed
choices.why: Not finding is not closing.

choices.text: As no known weakness, with the date it was checked
choices.why: Right: not closed, only not found yet.

choices.text: It is removed from the list
choices.why: The threat still exists.

choices.text: As a false positive, to be reopened if a scanner flags it
choices.why: Nothing showed it to be false.

prompt: Which kind of insider does carla's stage 4 note call the usual case?

choices.text: The malicious administrator who steals the database
choices.why: Possible, and not the usual case.

choices.text: The departed employee whose account still works
choices.why: Not in carla's note.

choices.text: The careless one
choices.why: Right, like a receptionist looking up a neighbour.

choices.text: The vendor with remote access
choices.why: Not in carla's note.

prompt: How many steps of the phishing path must be broken to stop it?

choices.text: All three
choices.why: A path needs every step to succeed.

choices.text: The first one, the phishing
choices.why: Any step will do, not only the first.

choices.text: The last one, closest to the records
choices.why: Any step will do.

choices.text: One, any of them
choices.why: Right, so stage 7 picks the cheapest.

prompt: What does the patient-password path reach?

choices.text: Every record, like the others
choices.why: It stops short of the goal.

choices.text: Exams, not clinical notes
choices.why: Right: notes are only in the console.

choices.text: Nothing, as passwords are hashed
choices.why: A leaked password from elsewhere still signs in.

choices.text: Only the patient's own bookings
choices.why: With T07, it reaches other patients' exams.

prompt: Which of these are ways stage 6 is done badly, according to the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: trying the paths on the live system
choices.why: That is a pentest by another name.

choices.text: copying generic attack patterns from a catalogue
choices.why: Paths have to come from facts about this system.

choices.text: drawing a control under each step
choices.why: That is the purpose: a map of where defences cut.

choices.text: starting from a goal stage 1 named
choices.why: That is how it should start.

prompt: Why did stage 7 put the phishing path above the forged webhook?

choices.text: Because phishing has more steps
choices.why: More steps is not more risk.

choices.text: Because the webhook is already fixed
choices.why: It is not.

choices.text: Because STRIDE listed it first
choices.why: STRIDE lists in no order of risk.

choices.text: It is being tried, it threatens clinical data, and its fix is cheap
choices.why: Right: likelihood from stage 4, impact from stage 1, cost from stage 6.

prompt: The risk that remains after the recommended countermeasures are in place is called ___ risk.

choices.text: Nobody had written that the integrity of exams matters
choices.why: Right, a gap in stage 1, fixed with a fifth objective.

choices.text: It is not a real threat
choices.why: It is: a wrong X-ray report is a clinical risk.

choices.text: Tampering threats never reach the objectives a business writes down
choices.why: This one does, once the objective exists.

choices.text: It was moved to lesson 5
choices.why: It stayed on the list.

prompt: The fifth objective Vereda added in stage 1 was: clinical records are ___.
At a small company, what does the lesson say PASTA typically changes?

choices.text: The number of threats, which roughly doubles after stage 4
choices.why: Stage 4 added context, not threats.

choices.text: The DFD
choices.why: Stage 3 reused lesson 2's drawing.

choices.text: The order of the threats, and the reasons for it
choices.why: Right. The list itself barely moves.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: The ranking and its reasons are new.

prompt: T07 and T09 ranked higher than their technical description suggested. Why?

choices.text: They are the easiest to exploit
choices.why: The lesson ranks by objectives, not ease.

choices.text: They have the highest CVSS scores
choices.why: No CVSS was used.

choices.text: Each threatens two objectives
choices.why: Right: private clinical data and the LGPD.

choices.text: daniel asked for them first
choices.why: The figure explains it, not a request.

prompt: In which situations does full PASTA pay for itself? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the people who decide what gets fixed are not technical
choices.why: The ranking comes with reasons in their terms.

choices.text: a large system that changes slowly
choices.why: The documents stay valid long enough.

choices.text: one feature that needs an answer this week
choices.why: STRIDE on its flows is an hour.

choices.text: nobody from the business will come
choices.why: Stages 1 and 7 become guesses.

prompt: What does the lesson call the shape Vereda kept?

choices.text: STRIDE inside a PASTA frame
choices.why: Right: stage 1 yearly, STRIDE in the middle, stage 7 for anything new.

choices.text: Full PASTA, every sprint
choices.why: That is the shape it rejected.

choices.text: STRIDE with no ranking
choices.why: It kept stage 7 to rank.

choices.text: PASTA stages 4 to 6 only, run by carla alone
choices.why: The business stages are the ones it kept.

prompt: Engineers run stages 1 and 7 alone because daniel is busy. What does the lesson say the result is?

choices.text: Better than nothing, and good enough
choices.why: The lesson calls it the wrong choice.

choices.text: Faster and just as good
choices.why: Faster, not as good.

choices.text: Invalid under the PASTA book
choices.why: The lesson's argument is about guesses, not rules.

choices.text: It looks authoritative and is as subjective as an unranked list
choices.why: Right: guesses about somebody else's priorities.

choices.text: Nothing, because scanners find bugs and models find flaws

choices.text: That T07 is confirmed, and private clinical data and the LGPD are at stake
choices.why: Right: the join leads from the CWE to the threat to the objectives.

choices.text: That a new threat must be added

prompt: Vereda considers a fourth path to every record: a backup copy kept by an outside company. Which stage first has to change?

choices.text: Stage 2, the technical scope
choices.why: Right: a new third party and a new copy of the data have to be in scope before they can be decomposed or attacked.

choices.text: Stage 7, since it is a new risk
choices.why: Stage 7 needs the stages before it.

choices.text: Stage 5, to find its CWE
choices.why: There is nothing to examine until it is in scope.

choices.text: None; backups are infrastructure
choices.why: A backup holds every record.
